title: Strings may run over several lines
body:
A string literal in `lang/lex.rs` closes at the next `"` and takes `\n` for a line break. A block of code or a long paragraph has to be written on one line with escapes.

## Proposal

A raw multi-line literal, for example `"""` ... `"""`. It keeps line breaks as written, drops the indent common to its lines, and takes no escapes. The formatter leaves its content untouched. The highlighter colors it as a string.

## Open

- The delimiter: `"""` reads naturally. A Rust-style `r#"..."#` allows any content.
close_reason: Landed uncommitted on dev: block() in crates/acre/src/lang/lex.rs reads a string between three quotes, keeps its lines, drops their shared indent and a break straight after the opening, and takes no escapes. The formatter leaves it as written (a test fixture checks this).
